video.title: The BORING Way to Make $1M/Year Without a College Degree

summary: David Heacock interviews Jim Baloga, CEO and owner of three US proprietary schools (Porter and Chester Institute, YTI Career Institute, College of Court Reporting) that train skilled trades, healthcare and court reporting students. Baloga explains how he bought the court reporting school as a small platform to avoid a large US Department of Education letter of credit, then used it to acquire the larger schools he had run for about 20 years. He covers tuition, outcomes, regulatory barriers to entry, upfront cash collection, low acquisition multiples and a roll-up plan. The host's takeaway is that deep industry experience reveals opportunities, and that a trade skill is a low-risk base for entrepreneurship.

speakers.name: David Heacock
speakers.description: Host of Boring Money, advocates trades and boring businesses

speakers.name: Jim Baloga
speakers.description: CPA by training, CEO and owner of Porter and Chester Institute, YTI Career Institute and College of Court Reporting

ideas.name: Accredited trade and healthcare school (Porter and Chester / YTI)
ideas.one_liner: Run accredited in-person vocational schools training electricians, HVAC techs, welders, nurses and others, funded largely by federal student aid.
ideas.business_model: Tuition per programme, about 80% paid via federal sources (Pell grants, direct loans, veterans benefits, state grants).
ideas.customer: School leavers, career changers and displaced workers (e.g. a 35-year-old ex-paralegal) wanting a skilled trade or healthcare career.
ideas.problem: Shortage of skilled tradespeople and mismatch between available jobs and trained talent; families want careers that AI will not replace.
ideas.offer: About one-year programmes with lectures plus hands-on industry-modeled labs, career services, job fairs and employer partnerships. Mantra: graduate on Friday, go to work on Monday.

pricing.notes: Some employer-sponsored programmes cost the student nothing (e.g. 10-week welding programme for a nuclear sub contractor).

acquisition_channels.details: Online marketing plus in-person referrals feed an admissions process; about 5-6,000 prospective students a year, about half enrol.
Students often start after seeing a friend's parent run a trade business; campus visits encouraged.
Employer partnerships and in-person career fairs with local contractors, hospitals and care facilities.

ideas.delivery: In-person campuses of 25,000-60,000 sq ft with labs (e.g. two-storey stick house for wiring), qualified instructors, curriculum, student finance and career services teams. About 350-400 employees, two-thirds in education.
unit_economics_claims: About 80% of tuition revenue from federal sources
Tuition collected upfront at start cycles about every 10 weeks
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; accreditation takes at least two years and a change of ownership may require a letter of credit of 25% of prior-year Title IV receipts.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: At least two years to become accredited for new entrants.

acquisition.how: Online marketing and lead gen can be largely automated, but admissions and in-person referrals need humans.

onboarding.how: Admissions, financial aid and enrolment involve counsellors and regulated paperwork.

delivery.how: Hands-on lab teaching by instructors on physical campuses.

billing.how: Student finance and aid disbursement can be systematised but are regulated and need staff.

support.how: Career services, job fairs and student retention are human-led.

uk_applicability.notes: Depends on US federal student aid and US accreditation. UK equivalents (FE colleges, apprenticeship providers, Ofsted, funding rules) differ entirely and are heavily regulated.

risks: Heavy regulatory exposure; one compliance foot-fault can be fatal
Student dropout and graduation/employment benchmark requirements (e.g. 55% graduation, 70% employed)

ideas.name: Acquire under-managed regulated schools and professionalise them (roll-up)
ideas.one_liner: Buy small, under-managed, accredited schools using a small-platform structure to avoid large letters of credit, then turn them around and bolt on more.
ideas.business_model: Acquire at 3-7x earnings, improve operations, grow revenue and EBITDA, use seller financing and cash flow post close.
ideas.customer: Aging school owners and operators looking to exit.
ideas.problem: Many proprietary schools are under-managed or mismanaged; buyers face a letter of credit equal to 25% of prior-year Title IV receipts on a change of control.
ideas.offer: Professional management and systems for acquired schools; Baloga bought the small College of Court Reporting first, then used it as a platform to buy the larger Porter and Chester ('David bought Goliath').

pricing.notes: Multiples were around 10x in 2000-2010. Lenders comfortable with 3-4x debt.

acquisition_channels.details: Deals sourced via industry relationships and private equity contacts (Thoma Bravo/Thoma Cressey).

ideas.delivery: Operator takes over, installs professional management, systems (CRM, student information) and compliance team.
unit_economics_claims: Court reporting school up over 50% since takeover
ideas.startup_cost: Nominal purchase for the small platform; letter of credit on a $50M Title IV school would be about $12.5M.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: About 5 years to find the regulatory pathway (talks from about 2017, closed July 2024).

acquisition.how: Deal sourcing relies on relationships and negotiation.

onboarding.how: Integration of acquired schools is human-led.

uk_applicability.notes: Structure is tied to US Department of Education rules; UK equivalent would be buying small training providers, a different regulatory regime.

risks: Regulatory approval of change of control

ideas.name: Online court reporting school (College of Court Reporting)
ideas.one_liner: Accredited online school training court reporters nationwide, based in Valparaiso, Indiana.
ideas.business_model: Tuition for online court reporting education, eligible for federal aid.
ideas.customer: Aspiring court reporters across the US.
ideas.problem: Many court reporting schools have closed; the school was under-managed.
ideas.offer: Online court reporting education delivered nationwide; school founded 1984.
ideas.delivery: Online education delivered to students across the country.
ideas.startup_cost: Nominal purchase amount, structured with PE backing.

acquisition.how: Online programme can use digital marketing.

onboarding.how: Admissions and aid still need staff.

delivery.how: Online delivery eases scaling but instructors are needed.

uk_applicability.notes: Court reporting and its accreditation/funding are US-specific, though online vocational training could be replicated with different rules.

quotes.text: there had been a number of court reporting schools that um, have just sort of gone away
quotes.speaker: Jim Baloga

ideas.name: Start a skilled trade business after training and experience
ideas.one_liner: Train in a trade, work 3-5 years under a licensed pro, then start or buy a trades business (electrical, plumbing, HVAC).
ideas.customer: Homeowners and commercial customers needing electricians, plumbers and HVAC techs.
ideas.problem: Demand exceeds supply; customers wait for plumbers and HVAC techs.
ideas.offer: Licensed trade services delivered by a skilled owner-operator, scalable to multiple trucks.
ideas.delivery: Technicians do on-site physical work; some grads run four or five trucks.
unit_economics_claims: Starting salaries about $60-65k for welders on nuclear sub programme
Licensing may need about 8,000 on-the-job hours
ideas.startup_cost: Cost of a one-year programme ($25-35k) plus experience.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Roughly 4-6 years including training and apprenticeship.

acquisition.how: Local SEO and Maps inbound can be automated.

support.how: Agents can handle bookings and queries.

uk_applicability.notes: Trades shortage and path (apprenticeship, then own business) apply in UK, with Gas Safe/NICEIC-type certifications instead of US licences.

tactics.name: Small-platform acquisition to dodge letter of credit
steps: Identify a small, under-managed accredited school with a low Title IV revenue base
Buy it first so the letter of credit is small
Use it as the acquiring platform for the larger target
Back with PE relationship and structure nominal purchase price

quote.text: David I bought David, and then David bought Goliath in a way that facilitated a unique transaction
quote.speaker: Jim Baloga

tactics.name: Employer-linked career pipeline
steps: Run in-person career fairs with local electrical, plumbing, HVAC firms and hospitals
Prepare students with resumes and interviews
Let employers hire on the spot

tactics.name: Deal structuring with low upfront capital
steps: Use seller financing to stretch payments

tactics.name: Cash-flow-positive tuition cycle
steps: Run start cycles about every 10 weeks
Negotiate trade credit terms for near-negative working capital

tactics.name: Campus real estate standardisation
steps: At lease renewal pick a high-traffic, highly visible site

warnings.warning: Over-leveraging in the 2000s boom drew regulatory attention and multiples collapsed.
Boom-bust enrolment tied to birth rates.

lessons.lesson: Deep time in an industry lets you spot opportunities outsiders cannot; the best path is often to work in a field for years before acquiring.

quote.text: a much better path is to work in an industry for a while until you have the knowledge
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Regulatory barriers to entry protect incumbents and create moats for skilled operators.
Test fast, fail fast, adjust fast, even in a regulated environment; the right structure took 3-5 years of trying.

quote.text: test fast, fail fast, and adjust fast, and doing it in the context of regulation
quote.speaker: Jim Baloga

lessons.lesson: Getting paid upfront gives a strong cash conversion cycle and can fund growth.
A trade skill de-risks entrepreneurship: worst case you return to working the trade, and student debt cannot be wiped by bankruptcy.
Structure acquisitions to use post-close cash flow and seller financing instead of outside capital.
Invest in mentoring and a flat functional structure so the CEO is not essential day to day.
AI-resistant, physical trades are attracting career changers and taking share from traditional higher education.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with real detail on regulation and deal structure, but few hard financials (no revenue/profit figures), and the interview is largely a conversational profile. The business is a US regulated school, not an agent-runnable business.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes boring-business content; guest promotes his schools and recruiting students.
